name: Rossi house
style: Dutch Colonial Revival (gambrel roof, full-width shed dormer)
materials: painted cedar shingles, sage green (#7A8C69), 5 in exposure
white painted trim, casings, Tuscan columns, K-style gutters
white 6-over-1 double-hung windows, mulled in threes and pairs
light grey architectural asphalt shingles; red brick chimneys
bluestone steps and landing, fieldstone piers with cast-stone urns
stained wood entry door with oval light, leaded sidelights, elliptical fanlight
notes: Main block 12.6 x 9.2 m, floor 0.75 m up, first-floor walls to 3.6 m, gambrel 64/22 deg with a 30 deg flared kick at the eave, ridge 8.3 m (Atlas 7.0 m; the gambrel needs the extra height). From the reference: sage shingles, the gambrel with the near full-width shed dormer (pairs left/right, a short triple in the middle), mulled triples of 6-over-1 windows, the arched gable portico on Tuscan columns, elliptical fanlight and sidelights, bluestone steps with fieldstone piers and urns, the flat-roofed side porch on the left, two ridge chimneys, white gutters and downspouts, foundation beds, white picket fence on the side. Interpreted: side and rear elevations, the plain rear gambrel, back stoop, asphalt driveway on the right to a parking pad, maple and dogwood. Neighbourhood not named in the register. Lot sides use corrected neighbor sides (site-specs.json neighbors_local x is mirrored): the Sullivan house is on the right (+39.7 m).
